blocks.text: src/workbench/observation.ts stores a bounded, non-authoritative read projection. Native keys include provider, type, scope and identifier. Caller workspace/principal scope is separately bound by the host. Duplicate events and lower source sequences do not regress state. Gaps and disconnects mark observations stale; reconnect alone does not establish current state. Only a real read-current snapshot restores confirmation.

blocks.text: Query indexes cover native references, invocation, typed relations, source basis, status kind, evidence, version and intervals. Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap. The benchmark in TRACEABILITY.md measures this model, not terminal viewport costs or live producer reconnect. Native reader adapters and entrypoint wiring need their own live evidence before observer release.

blocks.text: The external Furnace reader uses explicit bounded status/attempt/log-reference polling. The installed SDK's Run.events() follows one Attempt's output, not a Run lifecycle cursor stream, so that surface is not misrepresented as lifecycle reconnect. Read snapshots identify their sequential, non-atomic coherence. A closed or failed observer marks last-known state stale; stale readings cannot refresh confirmed projection state. Pi attachment is read-only and does not create, resume or stop a Run.
